newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-"AIR" JORDAN CAN STILL FLY WHEN HE WANTS TO.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-"AIR" JORDAN CAN STILL FLY WHEN HE WANTS TO.

text.p: Michael Jordan rarely hangs in the air anymore but proved he still can Wednesday in the Chicago Bulls' 97-85 romp over the Utah Jazz in Game 2 of the NBA Finals.
Along with his assortment of jump shots from all over the court, Jordan finally let loose with an evocative move late in the game.

He took the ball on the right wing, swooped past league Most Valuable Player Karl Malone along the baseline, double-clutched and spun one of his trademark reverse layups through the hoop -- left-handed.
"I've seen that so many times," said a smiling Scottie Pippen, who earlier in the game had dunked a clever Jordan look-away pass on a rare fast-break.
Jordan ended with 38 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists, two of them on three-pointers -- accounting for 58 points in all.
Playing down his personal heroics, Jordan lamented missing six out of his 21 free throws and insisted his intent throughout was to keep his teammates involved in the game.
"If I see Scottie (Pippen) limping, I'm not going to take all the responsibility myself. I'm going to ask the team to take some of that responsibility," Jordan said.
Jordan's starring effort was not lost on his opponents.
Jazz coach Jerry Sloan obviously was referring to Jordan when he suggested his players ought to have "fouled somebody, whoever they are."
Jordan's efficiency -- he was 11 of 20 from the field -- followed his dramatic game-winning shot in Game 1 Sunday. But most of his points are no longer scored in spectacular style.

Earlier in his career, Jordan spent much time defying gravity, improvising uncanny shots while hanging interminably in space. Nowadays, he will only occasionally hesitate in midair to watch a defender fall back to earth or to have time for a double-pump on a dunk.
Pippen, a teammate for nine seasons, said the 34-year-old Jordan still has all the hang time he needs.
"I think he's got everything in him that he's always had in the game since he's been a player at 23 or 24.
"It's just that now he has much more knowledge of the game, and so he doesn't have to pull those types of stunts as much," Pippen said.
